title: Ingroup as a “bodhisattva guild” (yes, really)
summary:
The most revealing part is how a goofy one-liner hardened into a full-on identity: @exgenesis drops “ingroup is actually a bodhisattva guild” and the whole TPOT/postrat neighborhood basically goes, *wait… that’s accurate*. It starts as a semi-ironic spiritual flex, but people keep treating it like a mission statement: a crew of smart internet weirdos trying to help each other (and maybe the world) wake up.

The prequel is @chercher_ai’s 2021 “Twitter Ecology” cluster maps—basically proof that this scene already existed as a tight like-network (“Downtown Postrats” with nodes like @visakanv and @exgenesis). The catalyst hits April 2022 when @exgenesis pitches “ingroup takes a vow of poverty and humility” to keep the community virtuous; @frideswyth and @loopholekid steer it into literal Buddhist vows, including a graphic of the Four Vows, and @exgenesis lands the punchline: “ingroup is just the largest bodhisattva crew in history.” A couple weeks later he reframes the whole thing as “we have… the greatest minds of our generation on a public twitter forum,” quoting the bodhisattva-guild tweet like it’s a banner.

Peak meme-to-movement happens in late 2023–2024 when @tasshinfogleman absorbs it into his Threadapalooza hero/empowerment riffing (“you may not know yet what kind of hero you are, but we do”), then institutionalizes it via his Service Guild work—explicitly calling Service Guild “a subset of tpot that is consciously aware of this and leaning into it.” The vibe doesn’t really “die” so much as it mutates: @no_no_nothing0 labels TPOT an “unintentional Twitter bodhisattva sect,” while @chercher_ai throws a sharp boundary flag (“when I talk about Bodhisattvas this is NOT what I mean”) amid discourse about people excusing abusive behavior under ‘wrathful bodhisattva’ rhetoric. Why care? Because it’s a case study in how online subcultures turn memes into moral self-concepts—and how that can be wholesome (mutual aid, mentoring, purpose) or dangerously self-justifying if nobody guards the line between “spiritual heroism” and enabling.
